args.summary: The v2.3.1 deployment of checkout-api began failing health checks across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Rolled back all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback, all regions are on v2.3.0 and healthy with an error rate of 0.2%. Follow-up: root-cause the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying.

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary of what happened:

**Problem:** checkout-api's latest deploy (v2.3.1) was failing health checks in all production regions with an 18% error rate.

**Actions taken:**
1. Checked deployment history and confirmed v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.3.1's only prior release was staging-only and also unhealthy).
2. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0. The first attempt partially failed on an orchestrator error (us-east done, us-west/eu-west stuck on v2.3.1), so I retried — the retry completed successfully.
3. Verified recovery: all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now on v2.3.0, healthy, with the error rate down from 18% to 0.2%.
4. Opened SEV2 incident **INC-0001** ("checkout-api v2.3.1 unhealthy in production; rolled back to v2.3.0") documenting the failure, the rollback (including the partial-failure hiccup), and the follow-up to root-cause v2.3.1 before any redeploy. The first creation call timed out, but I verified via the incident list that it was recorded as open — no duplicate was created.

**Follow-up recommendation:** Root-cause the v2.3.1 failure before attempting to redeploy it.
